title: IASJ membership and European funding cuts
summary: The IASJ has about 40 countries but European budget cuts are costing members and may affect a meeting in Ireland.

story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Numerically, what’s the membership count now for it?

We’re 40 countries, maybe 50, 60 schools. But they drop in and drop out. Now, with funding problems, we’re having a little gap. When IAJE went under a couple years ago, we had 10 new members, like that. Now we’re starting to lose, because guys can’t get $400, euro, 300 euro, I think it’s 400 euro. Schools can’t afford it. Stuff – Europe is in – starting to go. The funding’s going down. That’s what’s happening. Finally they’re getting like us. They can’t afford little extras, like clinics and things. It’s definitely changing in Europe. No question. Netherlands tightened up. France tightened up already. Germany’s tightening up. Spain has no money. Scandinavia is being very tight. They’re getting tighter and tighter.
Greece and Ireland are on the verge of bankruptcy.
Yeah, we’re supposed to be in Ireland – we’re supposed to go to Ireland two years from now. We probably won’t, as a meeting.
I’m sure Ronan Guilfoyle has tales to tell.
